title: England ‘do not have the same threat’ without Harry Kane, Thomas Tuchel says
content:
Thomas Tuchel admitted that England “do not have the same threat” without Harry Kane, but insisted that would be the case for any team in the world.

England have had two games without their captain Kane this international window, drawing 1-1 with Uruguay on Friday and then losing 1-0 to Japan on Tuesday night. Kane was scheduled to start against Japan but was withdrawn after pulling out of training in the build-up.

Tuchel said in his post-match press conference that England were not the same team without their record goalscorer, but said that Bayern Munich or any team in the world would miss a player that good. And that it was “just normal” to feel the absence of a world-class striker.

“In the absence of Harry Kane we don’t have the same threat,” Tuchel said. “Bayern Munich in the absence of Harry Kane has not the same threat. No team in the world has the same threat. It’s just normal. If top teams rely on top players, and top nations rely on top players, that’s just absolutely normal.”

These two games have raised questions about England’s effectiveness without Kane but Tuchel said that he was not worried about that, just over two months away from the World Cup.

“We can win games without Harry, we will win without Harry, we have won without Harry,” Tuchel said. “It’s easier to win matches with Harry.”

England changed their system for the Japan game with Phil Foden as a false 9, having initially used Dominic Solanke up front against Uruguay. Tuchel said that there is no point trying to find a “second Harry Kane” but said he was confident with the solutions England had prepared.

“We didn’t change the system against Uruguay and played with a no 9, ” he said.  “Today we played with a different no 9. And we played also with a 9 with Phil Foden and later with Dom Solanke. But I’m not looking for a second Harry Kane. There is no second Harry Kane. That’s also not an excuse, we were ready to beat Japan, we were ready to find solutions and to offer solutions to the team, but it was difficult, we struggled.”
